intro.title: Before buying, people search first.
intro.p1: Today, customers don't always discover a business from a storefront, a sign, or a friend's recommendation. Many look for information online before deciding to buy.
intro.p2: A website is the digital home of your business: the first place potential customers learn who you are, what you offer, and why your business deserves their choice.

benefits.title: What changes when your business has a website

rows.title: Trusted faster
rows.sum: Credibility, trust, and customer loyalty grow from a serious first impression.

items.text: An official web address (your own domain) looks more legitimate and trustworthy than a business that only uses social media accounts.
Modern consumers tend to assume a business with an online presence keeps better operating standards.
A website shows the owner takes the business seriously, and helps build a good relationship with customers.
The better customers know your brand, the greater their pride and loyalty.

rows.title: Found by new people
rows.sum: People who have never heard of your business can still find it through search.

items.text: A website works as a digital storefront: potential customers can look up information, browse a catalog, or buy at any time.
Not limited by physical location. Buyers from other cities, even other countries, can find your business.
Through SEO, your products or services can appear when people type keywords like “car wash near me”, “barbershop in your city”, or “traditional food catering”.
The people who arrive are actually looking for the solution or product you offer.

aside.text: a website does not automatically put your business on the first page of Google. But without a digital asset that can be found and optimized, the chance of being discovered organically is far more limited.

rows.title: Answering customer questions
rows.sum: An information hub that is always on, even when you're not holding your phone.

items.text: Prices, specifications, FAQs, and address are laid out clearly, so your customer service team has less to handle.
The easier it is for customers to get answers, the easier it is for them to act: call, send a WhatsApp message, order, or visit in person.
Buttons like “Buy Now”, “Book Online”, or “Contact on WhatsApp” let customers transact right away.

rows.title: Fully yours
rows.sum: Social media is great for interaction, but the space is controlled by someone else.

items.lead: Full control over content and brand.
items.text: Catalog, brand story, and look are arranged to fit your business's character, without competitor ads getting in the way as often happens on marketplaces.
A website is your own asset and doesn't depend on third-party platform policies.
Collect emails and WhatsApp numbers for direct promotions.
Install analytics tools like Google Analytics to see which products are most popular, where visitors come from, and how they shop.

slides.title: Dina's Journey with 'Yummy Cake'
slides.naration: Dina is a homemaker who is skilled at baking cakes. Her homemade treats are always in high demand in her neighborhood. Friends and neighbors often order birthday cakes, cookies, and dessert boxes for special occasions. Seeing the potential, Dina decides to start a small business called 'Lezatnya Dina'.

slides.title: Promoting on Social Media
slides.naration: At first, Dina relies solely on word-of-mouth recommendations. Over time, however, she realizes that her business is not growing. Her friends suggest promoting her cakes on social media. Dina creates Instagram and Facebook accounts to showcase photos of her baked goods. Soon, orders start coming in from beyond her neighborhood.

slides.title: A Big Order Lost
slides.naration: One day, Dina receives a large order inquiry from a potential customer who discovers her Instagram account. The customer wants to order 50 dessert boxes for a corporate event. However, the customer becomes confused because Dina relies entirely on Instagram direct messages. There is no comprehensive information about her menu, prices, or ordering process. Eventually, the customer chooses another bakery with a website that provides all the necessary information.

slides.title: Building a Landing Page
slides.naration: Dina realizes what her business is missing. She learns from a friend with digital industry experience and decides to create a simple landing page for her business. On the page, she showcases photos of her best cakes, a complete menu with prices, testimonials from satisfied customers, and an 'Order Now' button that connects directly to her WhatsApp.

slides.title: Outstanding Results
slides.naration: Once her landing page goes live, Dina shares the link on social media and in online ads. The results are remarkable! Many new customers feel more comfortable placing orders because all the information is available in one place. They no longer need to ask about prices or menu options. Dina even starts receiving orders from other cities thanks to online ads that direct potential customers to her landing page.

slides.title: Sarah's Online Course Business
slides.naration: Sarah is a digital marketing expert who decides to launch an online course business called 'SkillUp Academy'. She offers online courses in digital marketing, SEO, and content creation. Initially, Sarah relies solely on online course platforms to sell her classes. However, she feels that these platforms charge high commissions and limit her creativity in promoting her courses.

slides.title: An Engaging Webinar
slides.naration: One day, Sarah attends a webinar and gets the opportunity to promote her courses to hundreds of participants. She delivers an engaging presentation, and many attendees express interest in signing up. However, when Sarah provides only a link to the online course platform, many participants feel uncomfortable because they have to register and pay through that platform. Some even ask for a direct link to a website or dedicated page that provides more comprehensive information.

slides.title: Building a Landing Page
slides.naration: Sarah realizes the importance of having her own landing page. She quickly creates one for 'SkillUp Academy', featuring detailed descriptions of her courses, a list of modules and learning benefits, testimonials from previous students, and an 'Enroll Now' button that takes visitors directly to the payment process.

slides.title: Increasing Course Enrollments
slides.naration: Once her landing page goes live, Sarah begins promoting it through webinars, email marketing, and Facebook ads. As a result, course enrollments increase significantly because prospective students feel more comfortable and confident with the information available on her landing page.

stories.conclusion: From the narratives above, we can see that a landing page or website is an essential tool for businesses in the digital era. A landing page or website not only helps a business appear more professional but also makes it easier for customers to take action.

items.q: Does a website automatically show up on the first page of Google?
items.a: Not automatically. A website gives you an asset that can be found and optimized through SEO. Without that asset, the chance of being found organically is far more limited.

items.q: If I'm already active on social media, do I still need a website?
items.a: Social media is very useful for interacting with customers, but the platform is controlled by someone else. A website gives you more freedom to build your own brand experience.

items.q: Can the website be expanded after the basic package?
items.a: Yes. A website can grow with your business, for example with a product catalog, ordering system, blog, WhatsApp integration, newsletter, or a payment system.

items.q: What does the Basic Package include?
items.a: An official website with your business information: business profile, services, portfolio, and contact.
